easy.def: A huge snake that lives in the water.
examples: An anaconda is big.
The anaconda is long.
We saw an anaconda.

more.def: A very large snake of South America that lives in or near water and squeezes its prey.
examples: An anaconda slid into the river.
The anaconda is one of the largest snakes in the world.
Anacondas live in the rain forests of South America.

easy.def: A careful study of something to understand it.
examples: The scientist did an analysis.
Make an analysis.
The analysis was careful.

more.def: A careful study of something, looking at its parts, to understand it better.
examples: The scientist did an analysis of the water to see what was in it.
Our analysis of the story showed that the hero was brave.
The coach made an analysis of the game.

easy.def: To study something closely to understand it.
examples: We analyze the data.
The scientist analyzed the rock.
Let's analyze the story.

more.def: To study something carefully, looking at its parts, so that you can understand it.
examples: The scientists analyzed the water sample to see what was in it.
We analyzed the story to find the main idea.
The coach analyzed the video of the game to find ways to improve.

easy.def: A person in your family who lived a long time ago.
examples: My ancestor came from Italy.
We look at pictures of our ancestors.
An ancestor of mine.

more.def: A person in your family who lived long ago, such as a great-great-grandparent.
examples: My ancestors came to America on a ship from Ireland.
We made a family tree to learn about our ancestors.
One of my ancestors was a farmer.

easy.def: Your family from long ago.
examples: She knows her ancestry.
Their ancestry is Irish.
Ancestry is family history.

more.def: The family members who lived long ago and led to you.
examples: She learned about her family's ancestry.
Their ancestry goes back to Ireland.
The class traced their ancestry on a chart.

easy.def: A heavy metal hook that keeps a boat in one place.
examples: The ship dropped anchor.
The anchor is heavy.
The anchor sank.

more.def: A heavy metal tool on a rope or chain that holds a ship in place on the bottom of the water.
examples: The sailors dropped the anchor into the bay.
The anchor kept the boat from drifting.
The ship pulled up its anchor and sailed away.

easy.def: The man who leads the news on TV.
examples: The anchorman read the news.
An anchorman is on TV.
The anchorman talked.

more.def: The main man who reads the news on a TV or radio program.
examples: The anchorman read the evening news.
An anchorman introduced each story.
The anchorman talked about the storm.

easy.def: A small fish that is salty.
examples: An anchovy is a fish.
The pizza had anchovies.
An anchovy is small.

more.def: A tiny, salty fish that is used on pizzas and in salads.
examples: Dad put anchovies on the pizza.
An anchovy is smaller than your finger.
Large fish eat schools of anchovies.

easy.def: Very, very old.
examples: The ancient tree is older than my grandpa.
We saw an ancient castle.
This ancient coin is very old.

more.def: From a time very long ago, often thousands of years in the past.
examples: We saw ancient tools in the museum that people used long ago.
Ancient people painted animals on the walls of caves.
The ancient city was buried under sand for centuries.

easy.def: A word that joins things together.
examples: I like milk and cookies.
Mom and Dad are here.
We ran and jumped.

more.def: A word used to join words, groups of words, or sentences, showing that they go together or that one thing comes after another.
examples: We packed sandwiches, apples, and juice for the hike.
The sun set, and the stars slowly came out.
He studied hard and passed the spelling test.

easy.def: Again, in a new way.
examples: Let's start anew.
She began anew.
We will begin anew.

more.def: Again, in a new or fresh way.
examples: Let's start the game anew.
She began her drawing anew after the paper tore.
The farmer planted his garden anew in spring.

easy.def: A kind spirit with wings in stories.
examples: The angel had wings.
We saw a picture of an angel.
An angel is a helper.

more.def: In some religions and stories, a being who lives in heaven, often shown with wings.
examples: The angel in the story had white wings.
We saw a painting of an angel.
She wore a white dress and wings to play the angel.

easy.def: A very kind person.
examples: You are an angel for helping me.
My neighbor is an angel.
She was an angel with the baby.

more.def: A person who is very kind and good.
examples: Thank you for carrying my bag; you are an angel.
Our neighbor is an angel who brings us soup when we are sick.
The teacher is an angel with patient kids.

easy.def: Very good and sweet, like an angel.
examples: The baby looked angelic.
An angelic voice.
The angelic child slept.

more.def: Very kind, sweet and good, like an angel.
examples: The sleeping baby looked angelic.
She sang with an angelic voice.
The angelic child smiled sweetly.

easy.def: A strong feeling that makes you want to shout or fight.
examples: He shouted in anger.
Her face was red with anger.
Anger can make you say mean things.

more.def: A strong, hot feeling that you have when something seems unfair or wrong.
examples: He slammed the door in anger.
She counted to ten to calm her anger.
Anger can make you say things you do not mean.

easy.def: The corner shape where two lines meet.
examples: A square has four angles.
The angle is sharp.
The corner of the page is an angle.

more.def: The shape made where two lines or edges meet, measured in degrees.
examples: A square corner is a right angle.
The two lines made a sharp angle.
The picture hung at a strange angle.

easy.def: In an angry way.
examples: He shouted angrily.
She stomped angrily.
The bull snorted angrily.

more.def: In a way that shows you are angry.
examples: He shouted angrily at the dog.
She stomped angrily up the stairs.
The goose hissed angrily.

easy.def: Very mad.
examples: Dad is angry.
The angry bee buzzed.
She got angry.

more.def: Very upset at someone or something.
examples: He was angry when his sister broke his toy.
An angry wasp buzzed around my head.
She was angry that her game was canceled.

easy.def: Very strong pain or sadness.
examples: She cried in anguish.
His anguish was deep.
A cry of anguish.

more.def: Very great pain, sadness or worry.
examples: She cried out in anguish when she lost her toy.
His anguish was clear on his face.
The anguish of losing her pet showed on her face.

easy.def: A living thing that can move around.
examples: A dog is an animal.
Lions are animals.
The zoo has many animals.

more.def: A living thing that is not a plant, which can move and eats food.
examples: Every animal in the zoo gets fed twice a day.
A whale is the biggest animal in the sea.
The farm has many kinds of animals.

easy.def: Full of life, or made into a moving cartoon.
examples: The animated movie was fun.
She gave an animated talk.
The animated toy danced.

more.def: Full of life and energy, or made as a film of moving drawings.
examples: The animated film showed a dancing dog.
The two friends had an animated chat about the game.
She gave an animated talk with lots of hand waving.

easy.def: Drawings that seem to move.
examples: We watched an animation.
The animation was funny.
I like animation.

more.def: A film made by showing many drawings or pictures quickly so they seem to move.
examples: We watched an animation about a talking fish.
Making an animation takes thousands of drawings.
The class made an animation with clay figures.

easy.def: The joint between your foot and your leg.
examples: I hurt my ankle.
The sock goes over my ankle.
My ankle is sore.

more.def: The joint that joins your foot to your leg.
examples: I twisted my ankle at soccer.
The water came up to my ankles.
She wore a bracelet around her ankle.

easy.def: A chain or sock worn on the ankle.
examples: She wore an anklet.
The anklet is gold.
I lost my anklet.

more.def: A small chain or short sock worn around the ankle.
examples: She wore a silver anklet to the beach.
The anklet jingled as she walked.
I lost one anklet at the pool.

easy.def: A day you remember each year for something that happened.
examples: It is their wedding anniversary.
The school is having its tenth anniversary.
My parents celebrate their anniversary.

more.def: A day that you celebrate every year because something important happened on that date.
examples: My parents celebrate their anniversary with a special dinner.
The town is having a party for its hundredth anniversary.
It was the first anniversary of the library opening.

easy.def: To tell people something.
examples: The teacher will announce the winner.
She announced the news.
The principal announced a holiday.

more.def: To tell people something in a clear and public way.
examples: The principal announced the winner over the loudspeaker.
The captain announced that we were about to land.
She announced that dinner was ready.

easy.def: Something you tell everyone.
examples: The principal made an announcement.
The announcement was loud.
I heard the announcement.

more.def: A public statement that tells people something.
examples: The principal made an announcement about the snow day.
The announcement said the bus was late.
The announcement came over the loudspeaker.

easy.def: A person who tells people what is happening.
examples: The announcer called the names.
The radio announcer spoke.
The announcer said the game started.

more.def: A person who speaks on the radio, TV or a loudspeaker to tell people news or what is happening.
examples: The announcer called out the winner's name.
The radio announcer read the news.
The stadium announcer told us the score.

easy.def: To bother someone a little.
examples: Loud noise can annoy me.
Don't annoy the cat.
The fly annoyed us.

more.def: To make someone feel a little angry or upset by doing something again and again.
examples: The buzzing mosquito began to annoy everyone at the picnic.
Tapping your pencil on the desk will annoy the people around you.
It annoyed her when the song kept playing in her head.

easy.def: Something that bothers you.
examples: The noise was an annoyance.
I felt annoyance.
Flies are an annoyance.

more.def: Something that bothers or irritates you, or the feeling of being bothered.
examples: The noise was a small annoyance.
She sighed in annoyance at the long line.
Mosquitoes are an annoyance at the lake.

easy.def: Slightly angry or bothered.
examples: She was annoyed.
I am annoyed by the noise.
He was annoyed.

more.def: A little bit angry or bothered by something.
examples: She was annoyed when the music was too loud.
I am annoyed that I lost my pencil.
He was annoyed by the long wait.

easy.def: Bothering you.
examples: The buzzing fly is annoying.
The noise is annoying.
It is annoying to wait.

more.def: Making you feel a little angry or bothered.
examples: The buzzing fly was annoying.
The loud noise from the road was annoying.
It is annoying when the internet is slow.

easy.def: In a way that bothers you.
examples: The bell rang annoyingly.
He hummed annoyingly.
The dog barked annoyingly.

more.def: In a way that makes you feel annoyed.
examples: The fly buzzed annoyingly around my head.
The alarm rang annoyingly early.
The little brother annoyingly repeated everything.

easy.def: Happening once a year.
examples: We have an annual picnic.
The fair is annual.
It is an annual event.

more.def: Happening once every year.
examples: We go to the annual fair every fall.
The school holds an annual picnic.
The annual flood waters the fields.

easy.def: With no name given.
examples: The letter was anonymous.
An anonymous gift came.
The donor stayed anonymous.

more.def: Without the name of the person being known.
examples: An anonymous gift was left at the door.
The letter was anonymous, so we did not know who wrote it.
The donor wanted to stay anonymous.

easy.def: One more, or a different one.
examples: I want another cookie.
Pick another card.
She has another dog.

more.def: One more of the same kind, or a different one.
examples: Can I have another glass of water, please?
This path is blocked, so let us try another way.
We will play another game after lunch.

easy.def: What you say or write when someone asks you.
examples: I know the answer.
Her answer was yes.
What is the answer?

more.def: What you say or write back to a question, or the solution to a problem.
examples: The answer to the riddle is a clock.
I checked my answers before I handed in the test.
She gave a quick answer to the teacher's question.

easy.def: To say something back when asked.
examples: I answer the phone.
He answered Mom.
Please answer me.

more.def: To speak or write in reply to a question, call, or letter.
examples: Please answer the phone if it rings.
She answered every question on the quiz.
He knocked on the door, but nobody answered.

easy.def: A tiny insect that lives in big groups.
examples: An ant carried a crumb.
Ants live in a hill.
I saw an ant.

more.def: A very small insect that lives in large groups and works together.
examples: An ant carried a crumb back to the nest.
Ants build tunnels under the ground.
A long line of ants marched across the sidewalk.

easy.def: A fast animal like a deer with horns.
examples: An antelope ran.
The antelope is fast.
We saw an antelope.

more.def: A fast, graceful animal with horns that lives on grassy plains.
examples: An antelope raced across the plain.
The antelope has two long horns.
Antelopes can run faster than a horse.

easy.def: A metal rod that sends or receives radio or TV signals.
examples: The antenna is on the roof.
The radio has an antenna.
I moved the antenna.

more.def: A metal rod or wire that sends or receives radio, TV or phone signals.
examples: The TV antenna is on the roof.
The radio has a long antenna.
I moved the antenna to get a clearer picture.

easy.def: One of the two long, thin feelers on an insect's head.
examples: The ant waved its antenna.
A butterfly has antennae.
The antenna is thin.

more.def: One of a pair of thin feelers on the head of an insect, used to feel and smell.
examples: The ant waved its antennae.
A butterfly uses its antennae to sense the air.
The beetle's long antennae twitched as it walked.

easy.def: A special song for a country or a team.
examples: We sang the anthem.
The school has an anthem.
Stand for the anthem.

more.def: A special song that stands for a country, a school or a team and is sung on important occasions.
examples: Everyone stood and sang the national anthem before the game.
The school anthem is about courage and kindness.
The team's anthem played over the speakers.

easy.def: A little mound of dirt that ants make.
examples: I saw an anthill.
Ants live in the anthill.
The anthill is small.

more.def: A small mound of dirt built by ants over their nest.
examples: I stepped around the anthill.
Thousands of ants lived in the anthill.
The anthill was at the edge of the lawn.

easy.def: A medicine that kills germs.
examples: The doctor gave me an antibiotic.
An antibiotic helps.
Antibiotics kill germs.

more.def: A medicine that kills germs and cures some illnesses.
examples: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my ear.
Antibiotics kill bacteria but not viruses.
She took the antibiotic for a week.

easy.def: Medicine that kills germs that make you sick.
examples: The doctor gave me antibiotics.
Antibiotics fight germs.
I took antibiotics.

more.def: Medicines that kill or stop harmful germs called bacteria in the body.
examples: The doctor gave me antibiotics for my ear infection.
Antibiotics fight germs that make you sick.
You have to take all of your antibiotics, even when you feel better.

easy.def: To expect something.
examples: I anticipate a surprise.
We anticipated rain.
She anticipated the question.

more.def: To expect something and be ready for it.
examples: We anticipated rain, so we packed umbrellas.
She anticipated my question and had an answer ready.
The coach anticipated the play.

easy.def: Looking forward to something that will happen.
examples: I waited with anticipation.
She felt anticipation.
The kids jumped in anticipation.

more.def: The feeling of excitement that you have when you are waiting for something good to happen.
examples: The children waited in anticipation for the circus to begin.
She felt a rush of anticipation on the morning of her birthday.
In anticipation of the storm, we put the chairs inside.

easy.def: Funny, silly things that someone does.
examples: The clown's antics were funny.
The puppy's antics made us laugh.
We laughed at his antics.

more.def: Playful, silly behavior that makes people laugh.
examples: The clown's antics made the children giggle.
We laughed at the puppy's antics in the yard.
The monkey's antics delighted the crowd.

easy.def: Something that stops the bad effects of a poison.
examples: The doctor gave an antidote.
An antidote can help after a bite.
He took the antidote.

more.def: A medicine that stops the harmful effects of a poison or a bite.
examples: The doctor gave her an antidote after the snake bite.
Hospitals keep an antidote ready for certain kinds of poison.
Laughter can be an antidote to a bad mood.

easy.def: A very old, valuable thing.
examples: The clock is an antique.
Grandma collects antiques.
The antique chair is old.

more.def: An object that is very old and often valuable, such as furniture.
examples: The clock is an antique from the 1800s.
The antique dealer sold old clocks.
We looked at antique furniture in the shop.

easy.def: A medicine that kills germs.
examples: The nurse used antiseptic.
Antiseptic cleans cuts.
Put antiseptic on it.

more.def: A substance that kills germs, used to clean cuts and scrapes.
examples: The nurse cleaned the cut with antiseptic.
Antiseptic stings a little but keeps germs away.
Mom put antiseptic on my scraped knee.

easy.def: A hard horn that grows on a deer's head.
examples: The deer has antlers.
The antler is big.
We found an antler.

more.def: One of the hard, branched horns that grow on the head of a deer.
examples: The buck's antlers are wide and sharp.
We found a shed antler in the woods.
Moose grow large antlers every year.

easy.def: Restless and unable to sit still.
examples: I feel antsy.
The antsy kids moved.
He is antsy.

more.def: Restless and eager to move, as if you have ants in your pants.
examples: I felt antsy during the long car ride.
The antsy kids could not sit still.
He was antsy waiting for the bell.

easy.def: A heavy iron block that a blacksmith hammers on.
examples: The blacksmith used an anvil.
The anvil is heavy.
The anvil is iron.

more.def: A heavy block of iron on which metal is hammered into shape.
examples: The blacksmith hammered the hot iron on the anvil.
An anvil is very heavy.
Sparks flew from the anvil.

easy.def: A feeling of worry.
examples: She felt anxiety before the test.
The anxiety grew.
His anxiety was high.

more.def: A nervous feeling about what might happen.
examples: She felt anxiety before the big test.
His anxiety eased when he saw his mom.
Deep breaths can help calm anxiety.

easy.def: Worried and nervous.
examples: I am anxious before a test.
She felt anxious.
The dog looked anxious.

more.def: Feeling worried or uneasy about what might happen.
examples: I felt anxious before the big test.
She was anxious about meeting her new teacher.
The anxious dog paced by the door.

easy.def: One or some, it does not matter which.
examples: Do you have any gum?
Pick any card.
I do not see any bugs.

more.def: Some, or one of a group when it does not matter which one.
examples: Do you have any questions about the story?
You can choose any book from the shelf.
We could not find any mud, so we went inside.

easy.def: Any person at all.
examples: Is anybody home?
I do not see anybody.
Anybody can come.

more.def: Any person at all, no matter who.
examples: Anybody can learn to draw with enough practice.
Did anybody see where my hat went?
The pool is open to anybody who lives in town.

easy.def: In any case.
examples: It rained, but we went anyhow.
I was tired, but I played anyhow.
She is shy but sang anyhow.

more.def: In any case, or no matter what.
examples: It was raining, but we went to the park anyhow.
He was tired, but he finished anyhow.
I know it is hard, but let's try anyhow.

easy.def: Not now, not any longer.
examples: I do not play anymore.
She does not live here anymore.
It does not hurt anymore.

more.def: Any longer, now, used with a negative.
examples: I do not play with that toy anymore.
The shop does not sell candy anymore.
The pain is gone and it does not hurt anymore.

easy.def: Any person at all.
examples: Can anyone help?
I do not see anyone.
Anyone can come.

more.def: Any person at all, no matter who.
examples: Anyone can learn to swim with enough practice.
Did anyone see my blue jacket?
The library is open to anyone who wants to read.

easy.def: Any thing at all.
examples: I will eat anything.
Do you see anything?
She can do anything.

more.def: Any thing at all, no matter which one.
examples: You can ask me anything about dinosaurs.
I could not find anything to eat in the cupboard.
He is brave and will try anything once.

easy.def: At any time.
examples: Come over anytime.
You can call me anytime.
Visit anytime you like.

more.def: At any time at all, whenever you like.
examples: You can borrow a book from the library anytime.
Come visit us anytime this summer.
Call me anytime you need help.

easy.def: Even so.
examples: It rained, but we went anyway.
I was scared, but I did it anyway.
She is small, but she won anyway.

more.def: In spite of something, or whatever else is true.
examples: It was raining, but we played outside anyway.
He was nervous but sang the song anyway.
The shirt was too big, but she wore it anyway.

easy.def: In any place.
examples: I can sit anywhere.
We can go anywhere.
I cannot find it anywhere.

more.def: In or to any place at all.
examples: You can sit anywhere you like.
I looked for my shoe, but could not find it anywhere.
We could go anywhere for vacation.
